title: Sheinbaum Says Chicoasén II Will Have the World’s Largest Bulb Turbines Without Displacing Communities
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by[La Jornada Editorial
Staff](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/La%20redacci%C3%B3n) originally
appeared in the [November 11, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/11/politica/chicoasen-ii-
tendra-las-turbinas-bulbo-mas-grandes-del-mundo-sin-desplazar-pueblos-
sheinbaum), Mexico’s premier left wing daily newspaper._

In a format she called _Science in a Minute in the Field_ , President Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo explained on her social media this Wednesday how the bulb
turbines that the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) is installing at the
Chicoasén II hydroelectric plant in Chiapas work, a technology that harnesses
water without the need for a large dam.

In videos released this Wednesday and recorded during the president’s tour of
the state last weekend, a CFE specialist explained from the intake structure
that the plant will have **three bulb units of 80 megawatts each** , “the
largest in the world.”

He explained that the water flows along the outside to the runner blades,
whose rotation drives the generator’s rotor. Once in operation, the structure
will be flooded and access will be through hatches to maintain the
turbogenerator. “And that is how a bulb turbine works,” the president
concluded.

> [Post by @Claudiashein on
> X](https://twitter.com/Claudiashein/status/2120655147730923909)

In another video, posted on X, Sheinbaum described the project as “a great
technological innovation.”

> “We are building a hydroelectric plant that sits in the riverbed, that does
> not require a large dam or the displacement of communities.”
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

Chicoasén II will have a **capacity of 240 megawatts** and will reuse water
that has already passed through turbines. It is located downstream from the
Manuel Moreno Torres plant, known as Chicoasén, on the Grijalva River.
According to the CFE, **more than 1,500 workers** are working on the project,
and the program includes roads, educational infrastructure and
electrification. The company expects the plant to reach **full capacity by
late 2028**.

“Recovering national sovereignty, long live the women and men who work at the
CFE,” the president concluded.
